14.author: St. Gregory of Nyssa
14.text: For Gregory of Nyssa, the burning bush is the first glimpse of the central paradox of Christian contemplation: God is known truly, yet remains incomprehensible. When the Lord names Himself 'I Am' to Moses, He reveals that He alone exists in the proper sense. Every creature has being only by participation in Him. Gregory builds his entire mystical theology on this distinction. To know God is to keep advancing into His infinite life, never arriving, always discovering. He calls this the soul's perpetual stretching forward, an unending growth into the divine that is itself the goal.
